review_metadata.scope: Security review of examples/v4 for PR #1 after commit a53f3eb375823bd932e693cb162f9cbb677fc7f5. Reviewed the nested examples/v4 git range 070dea5c5d746859f28ba9e061ba442975a0db53..a53f3eb375823bd932e693cb162f9cbb677fc7f5, with focus on auth, tenant scope, local-only exposure, CORS, SQL/XSS/injection paths, OpenRouter proxy behavior, secret handling, filesystem/command sinks, network calls, logging, and unsafe side effects.

no_findings_rationale: Reviewed the requested nested PR range and the sensitive implementation surfaces at head a53f3eb375823bd932e693cb162f9cbb677fc7f5: backend configuration, startup, route handlers, SQLite persistence, error shaping, OpenRouter client and SSE decoder, frontend API client, chat rendering, environment defaults, README, gitignore, and tests. The backend rejects non-loopback BIND_ADDR values before binding, so the unauthenticated API is intentionally scoped to local use. Browser-based cross-origin writes are not exposed by the changed code because mutating routes require application/json, invalid JSON is rejected before persistence or provider calls, and CORS permits only the configured frontend origin. Conversation/message data is single-user local state; there is no claimed tenant boundary to bypass beyond the enforced loopback service boundary. Request-controlled conversation ids, titles, and message content reach SQLite only through sqlx bind parameters, and I found no dynamic SQL construction from user input. I found no request-controlled filesystem access, command execution, or provider URL selection. The OpenRouter outbound host is environment-configured, while user input is serialized only into the provider request body. OPENROUTER_API_KEY remains backend-only and is attached only through reqwest bearer_auth; .env.example and README contain placeholders, and .gitignore excludes real env files and local database artifacts. Client-visible provider and database errors are sanitized through public_message/detail paths and do not include authorization headers, upstream response bodies, SQL internals, prompts, or secrets. Frontend user messages render as React text, assistant markdown renders through react-markdown with remark-gfm only, and I found no rehypeRaw, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, eval, or innerHTML sink. The a53f3eb delta only adds a TanStack Query cache fallback for already delivered stream messages when recovery refetch fails; it does not add a new trust boundary, network target, secret sink, filesystem sink, command sink, HTML sink, or authorization decision. I found no exploitable auth bypass, confused deputy, path traversal, command injection, SSRF, XSS, SQL injection, secret exposure, unsafe default, broad permission, or sensitive side effect with a concrete abuse path in the requested commit range.
false_positive_notes: The API is unauthenticated, but the reviewed app documents and enforces a loopback-only single-user service boundary and has no tenant or account model; I did not treat lack of bearer/session auth as an exploitable authorization bypass without a remote or cross-origin abuse path.
OPENROUTER_BASE_URL and DATABASE_URL are environment-controlled and could be unsafe if an attacker controls process configuration, but they are not request-controlled inputs in this application.

Local same-host processes can call loopback services directly; that is outside the documented browser-facing local development boundary and was not reported without evidence of a stronger intended local-user isolation guarantee.

The repository-level codedungeon rules status command reported stale in this outer checkout, but this persona artifact preserves the task-provided approved project rules envelope. The reviewed nested examples/v4 PR metadata targets the requested head a53f3eb375823bd932e693cb162f9cbb677fc7f5.

rubric_self_check.authn_authz: No actionable auth finding under the documented local-only single-user workflow. backend/src/config.rs rejects non-loopback binds and backend/src/routes.rs restricts browser CORS to the configured frontend origin.
rubric_self_check.tenant_scope: No multi-tenant authorization model is implemented or claimed. The reviewed data access model is local single-user conversation storage guarded by the loopback bind boundary.
rubric_self_check.secrets: No real OpenRouter key or other credential was found in reviewed tracked source, .env.example, README snippets, frontend code, or the provider proxy path. The key is read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY in backend config and used server-side only.
rubric_self_check.network_ssrf: OPENROUTER_BASE_URL can be changed by environment configuration, but it is not request-controlled. User-controlled messages cannot select the outbound host or headers.
rubric_self_check.sql_injection: Reviewed SQLite queries use sqlx bind parameters for request-controlled values. No string-built SQL from title, message content, or conversation id was found.
rubric_self_check.xss: React escapes user message text. Assistant content is rendered through react-markdown with remark-gfm only, with no raw HTML plugin or direct HTML sink in the reviewed frontend.
rubric_self_check.filesystem_commands: No request-controlled filesystem access or command execution sink was found.
rubric_self_check.logging_errors: AppError and StreamEvent error paths return generic database/provider messages. TraceLayer is used for HTTP tracing, and reviewed source does not log API keys, Authorization headers, prompts, provider bodies, or SQL errors to clients.
rubric_self_check.sensitive_side_effects: Provider setup failures occur before persisting a user turn. Mid-stream provider failures yield sanitized errors and return without storing an assistant message; empty assistant output is rejected. The a53f3eb cache fallback only mirrors already delivered user-message data into client cache after a failed recovery refetch.
